meta.title: Ondra Process Host
meta.description: Subprocess hosting: hand argv, cwd, stdio dispositions and a grace period explicitly to the upstream subprocess seam, restart once within a budget when the child dies, and tear down through the provider's managed process range instead of signalling by hand. It deliberately never kills by pid: POSIX scopes and Windows job objects are exactly the layer where hand-rolled signalling leaves grandchildren alive, so reimplementing it would mean rewriting the job object. It equally refuses the detached half of the requirement - a child that outlives its parent has nobody to reap it after the plugin unloads, and the leftover process holds the port, the pid file goes stale, and the next start fails with an address already in use. The pid file only does what can be done: the upstream handle exposes no process id, so one is written when available and no file is created otherwise, since a fabricated id is far worse than a missing file - whatever reads it would kill an unrelated process. Restarts carry a generation number, so a late callback from an old handle cannot mark the new child as crashed. Stopping reports the termination request and the confirmed silence separately, because the request is not the fact. Every method returns instead of throwing: hosting failure is normal, and callers should not have to choose whether to wrap it. There is no timer, no socket, and no log passthrough; collected output is capped and never forwarded into the host's own stream.
